sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is initialized lazily upon first access.
sketches.resonance: Declaring someone as an `object` means there can only ever be one of them, and they come into existence only when you reach for them.

sketches.mechanism: A `weak` reference does not prevent deallocation — the thing you hold can vanish at any moment, becoming `nil` without warning.
sketches.resonance: Loving weakly means the one you hold onto can disappear at any time, and you must always check if they are still there.

sketches.mechanism: The `ensure` block runs whether the code succeeds or fails — it executes unconditionally, even after an exception.
sketches.resonance: No matter what happens — success, failure, catastrophe — the `ensure` block is the one thing that will always run, the promise that cannot be broken.
sketches.draft:
begin
  raise
rescue
  retry if false
ensure
  remember
end
